description: Verify that DUT TCP increases exponentially the interval between successive zero-window probes (RFC 1122 §4.2.2.17)
approach:
[Objective]
Like RTO backoff, zero-window probes back off exponentially to reduce stress on a peer that's persistently full. RFC 1122 §4.2.2.17 says SHOULD double.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Handshake → data → zero-window state.
2. Probe #1, #2, #3 emitted; tester remains in zero-window.
3. Observation: Δt(probe2-probe1) > initial RTO; Δt(probe3-probe2) > Δt(probe2-probe1).

[Pass condition]
Probe intervals strictly grow.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_seg1 — first data segment missing
• Fail_no_probe<n> — probe n missing
• Fail_probe2_not_doubled — probe 2 delta not greater than initial RTO
• Fail_probe3_not_doubled — probe 3 delta not greater than probe 2 lower bound

verdicts.Pass: DUT zero-window probe intervals doubled — normal
verdicts.Fail_probe2_not_doubled: Probe 2 delta not greater than initial probe RTO
verdicts.Fail_probe3_not_doubled: Probe 3 delta not greater than probe 2 lower bound
